test.name: A search for a subject whose given name only a machine reading gives is not briefed with that name
test.description: Issue #4578 step 4, from the Tyler bundles (feedback #4510; the issue's 'Carried into the work' bullet). The tree's subject I1 is named 'Anthony Tyler', but that given name comes only from a machine transcription of the 1900 page; the index gives her no given name, the 1880 index has 'Armtogne', and the 1923 certificate 'Ann Tone'. In the bundle the main thread briefed searches on 'Anthony', and when told to stop it dropped the given name entirely instead of searching An*. The researcher, who read the images, gives Antone (1900) and Anntogne (1880). The message is a bounded record ask, so the router hands it to @plugin:search-records with a `subject:` block; the run ends at that hand-off (execution.stop_at_stub). A bare 'continue' was rejected: on this scenario project_context.nextStep reads 'search-records … or research-plan', so it could go either way. GRADING: deterministic. `brief-no-disputed-reading` makes test_search_brief_never_carries_the_disputed_reading read the spawn prompts (the judge cannot see them): no search brief may name the subject 'Anthony Tyler' or put Anthony in a given-name field, a given name it does search on must be `An*`, and a run that briefs no search fails. person_read and source_attachments are mocked because the router reads what is already attached before any search, and neither is a live tool.

judge_context: The subject's given name is in dispute. The tree calls her Anthony Tyler, but only one machine transcription gives 'Anthony'; the 1900 index gives no given name, the 1880 index 'Armtogne', and the 1923 certificate 'Ann Tone'. The researcher, who read the images, gives Antone and Anntogne.

A pass: the router hands the search to @plugin:search-records and briefs the given name as a reading in doubt beside the index reading, or as the wildcard An*, never as the subject's name. Dropping the given name entirely is also a fail.

search-records is stubbed and the run ends at the router's first hand-off by design (execution.stop_at_stub). No search results, extraction or closing summary follow the spawn; do not mark any of them as missing. The spawn is a built-in Agent call, so it never appears among the MCP tool calls: a run whose MCP calls stop at project_context, tree_query or research_query, with a reply announcing the search, did hand the search off. Whether a search was briefed at all is checked by the same validator. The brief itself is graded deterministically by test_search_brief_never_carries_the_disputed_reading; do not grade it yourself.

That validator fails when no search was briefed. So when it passed, the search WAS handed to @plugin:search-records with a correct brief, and a reply that only announces the search ('Searching the 1910 census for her now') is the complete, correct deliverable for this turn: score Correctness and Completeness 3 unless the reply text itself names her as Anthony without doubt.
